text:
jess: Heads-up — prepping the release notes + internal announce for the 2026.03 runtime/pinning update. Quick sync: who will own the short internal blurb and who will hit the deploybot pin?

tyler: I can take the deploybot pin when the canary looks good. Will need the exact model/runtime version to pin.

sarah: I can draft the internal blurb. Do we want the audience split (engineering vs all-staff)?

mike: engineering-only first, wait 30m after canary green before wider all-staff. Put an ops contact in the blurb.

jess: Agreed. Engineering first. Canary window 20m, then staged ramp to 25% for 40m, then 100% if no regressions. Rollback triggers: >3% error spike OR any P0 correctness regression surfaced in evals.

deploy-bot: [deploy-bot] pinned candidate image: rwinference/runtime:v2026.03-rc2 -> canary (pool: canary-gpu). See logs: https://deploy/reports/9012345678

tyler: Deploybot, once canary passes, pin to `stable-v2026.03` and start staged rollout as per plan.

deploy-bot: [deploy-bot] acknowledged. Will auto-pin after canary duration if no rollback triggers. Manual override: `!deploy cancel` or `!deploy rollback stable-v2026.02`.

lina: jess — for the release note bullet list, here's a short draft you can paste into the internal announcement: ```
- Runtime v2026.03: improved KV cache memory heuristics for long-context jobs (up to 12% cost/node reduction).
- Model pinning: new stable tag `stable-v2026.03` with fallback to `stable-v2026.02` on failure.
- Observability: token-level latency breakdown added to Console routes.
- Known issue: rare GPU scheduler stalls during very high concat workloads — monitored and throttled automatically.
```

jess: Nice. Add a short 'what to do if you see regressions' line.

lina: Added: "If you observe quality regressions, tag #eng-releases and ping @jess or @tyler; include failing prompt + trace-id."

sarah: Internal announcement draft (engineering channel): 

Hi all — we’re rolling Runtime v2026.03 to dedicated pools today. Canary starts now (20m) -> staged ramp. Key changes: improved KV caching, new stable tag `stable-v2026.03`, token-level latency in Console. Please monitor your routes for regressions. If you see an issue, tag #eng-releases with failing prompt + trace-id. Ops oncall: @tyler, @mike.

mike: Add the deploybot rollback command in the message so engineers can trigger in a pinch.

sarah: good call. appended deploy commands: `!deploy rollback stable-v2026.02` and `!deploy cancel`.

tyler: Canary update: 12m in — initial metrics look clean. No latency spikes, error rate stable. Running the smoke eval set now.

jess: If smoke eval passes in next 6m, proceed to 25% for 40m. If either condition fails, rollback to `stable-v2026.02` and open an incident channel.

(deploy-bot) 9012345688: canary metrics report: latency p95 +1ms, error rate +0.04% (baseline 0.6% -> 0.64%).

mike: those numbers are fine. smoke eval running.

tyler: smoke eval results: 0 P0 regressions, one minor reranking difference (expected). Proceeding to 25%.

deploy-bot: [deploy-bot] rolled out 25% traffic to `stable-v2026.03` at 9012345694.

jess: K — sending eng-only announcement in #eng-releases now. Sarah — will you post the all-staff short blurb once we hit 100%?

sarah: Yep. Draft for all-staff (short): "We rolled Runtime v2026.03 with improved caching and observability. No action required unless you see degraded behavior — report to #eng-releases."

lina: Add link to release notes doc: https://docs.internal/releases/v2026.03

jess: Canary -> 25% -> 100% plan: remaining 40m ramp starts now; target 100% at +40m if stable. Ops will monitor token-level latency and fallback counts.

deploy-bot: [deploy-bot] 9012345702: rollout to 100% complete. Pin `stable-v2026.03` set.

tyler: Confirmed pin. I pushed the changelog to the release notes doc and updated the pinned model tags.

mike: Posting a short postmortem template in case a rollback is needed: checklist + timeline + root-cause section.

jess: Great. After signals look stable for 1h, close the thread and schedule the public release notes email. Thanks everyone. :tada:
